Why go: a jungle course high in Samui's hills

Koh Samui has several zipline parks; this one stands out for its setting. It sits high in the island's central hills next to Tan Rua waterfall, and mixes ziplines with rope bridges between the trees, so the hour on the course feels like crossing the forest rather than sliding down a hillside. The included transfer matters, because the road up is steep and not one to attempt on a scooter.

What you'll do

A van collects you from the main beach areas and climbs into the hills. After a safety briefing and harness fitting you work through 10 ziplines and a series of tree bridges with guides clipping you in at each platform. Afterwards there is about half an hour to walk to the waterfall, around 200 m away, or sit at the café before the drive back.

Who it suits

  • Families with children from 6: the course is guided and paced for beginners.
  • Couples and groups who want a 2–3 hour activity that fits around a beach day.
  • Anyone who wants to see the green interior of the island.

Who should choose something else

  • Anyone pregnant, over 120 kg or uncomfortable with heights.
  • Visitors who want a longer adventure day: a jeep safari or the ATV ride at Lipa Noi covers more ground.

Good to know

  • Driving yourself: the access road is steep and rough; if you drive, use a 4x4 or pickup truck, not a scooter.
  • Clothing: closed shoes and shorts or trousers; tie back long hair and leave loose jewellery in the hotel.
  • Season: the waterfall is fullest from October to January; the course is cooler in the 09:30 slot.
